rounds.note: Mostly fine. Main worry is latency and silent degradation.

quote.exact: sequentially, so its latency adds straight onto the feed request
quote.prefix: The habit call runs after the Tardis fetch,

messages.author: you
messages.body: Why sequential? Could this run alongside `Tardis.Fetch`? Both only need the user id as far as I can tell.

messages.author: agent
messages.body:
It could. Both calls depend only on `req.UserID`; the author kept them sequential to reuse the error branch at [request_builder.go:47](rr:code/pkg/ranker/request_builder.go#L47-49).

| path | p50 | p99 |
|---|---|---|
| Tardis.Fetch | 4 ms | 18 ms |
| habit.RecentEvents | 3 ms | 12 ms |
| **sequential** | 7 ms | **30 ms** |
| **parallel** | 4 ms | **18 ms** |

I added a section with an errgroup sketch instead of repeating it here:

![](rr:doc/parallel-sketch)

messages.author: you
messages.body: Shouldn't this bump a `habit_degraded_total` counter? Otherwise a 100% failure is invisible.

messages.author: agent
messages.body: Agreed. `b.metrics` is already injected ([NewBuilder](rr:code/pkg/ranker/request_builder.go#L32)), so it's one line — the sketch in [Parallel fetch sketch](rr:doc/parallel-sketch) includes it. I'd suggest it to the author as a required change.

messages.author: you
messages.body: `ts` here is a timestamp but the proto says `ts_ms`. Where does the conversion happen?

messages.author: agent
messages.body:
In `decode`: TFS returns epoch millis in the `ts` column and it's copied straight into `TsMs`.

![](rr:code/pkg/features/habit/fetcher.go#L39-47)

The SQL table is the offline sink; the online path never reads it.

messages.author: you
messages.body: Can we also cover the degrade branch in `Build`? A stub fetcher that errors should still yield a request with empty `HabitEvents`.
